ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in Figure 1, select a fixed point O in the plane and draw a directed ray $Ox$. By choosing a unit length, the position of any point M on the plane can be determined by the degree $\theta$ of $\angle MOx$ and the length m of $OM$, forming an ordered pair $\left(\theta, m\right)$, which is referred to as the "polar coordinates" of point M. The coordinate system established in this manner is called the "polar coordinate system".

Application: Given a polar coordinate system as in Figure 2, if a regular hexagon has a side length of 2 and one side OA lies on the ray $Ox$, what would be the polar coordinates of the vertex C of the hexagon?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw CB$\perp$OA at point B,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OBC=$90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ the side length of the regular hexagon is 2,\\
$\therefore$ OA=CA=2, $\angle$OAC=$120^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$COA=$\angle$OCA=$\angle$ACB=$30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ AB=$\frac{1}{2}$AC=1, BC=$\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ OC=2BC=2$\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore$ the polar coordinates of vertex C of the regular hexagon should be $\boxed{(30^\circ, 2\sqrt{3})}$.

By choosing a unit length, the position of any point M on the plane can be determined by the degree \(\theta\) of \(\angle MOx\) and the length \(m\) of \(OM\), forming an ordered pair \((\theta, m)\), which is referred to as the polar coordinates of point M. The coordinate system established in this manner is called the polar coordinate system.

Application: Given a polar coordinate system as in Figure 2, if a regular hexagon has side length 2 and one side \(OA\) lies on the ray \(Ox\), what are the polar coordinates of vertex \(C\) of the hexagon?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: As shown in the figure, draw \(CB \perp OA\) at point \(B\). Therefore \(\angle OBC = 90^\circ\). Because the side length of the regular hexagon is 2, \(OA = CA = 2\), and \(\angle OAC = 120^\circ\). Therefore \(\angle COA = \angle OCA = \angle ACB = 30^\circ\). Thus \(AB = \frac{1}{2}AC = 1\), \(BC = \sqrt{3}\), and \(OC = 2BC = 2\sqrt{3}\). Therefore, the polar coordinates of vertex \(C\) are \((30^\circ, 2\sqrt{3})\).

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In Figure 2, a regular hexagon is drawn, point O is at the origin, side OA is along the positive x-axis direction, A is located near x=2, C is the upper-right vertex adjacent to A, and OC is slanting upward to the right. From the figure, it can be known that this is a regular hexagon with side length 2, and OA is one of its sides.
Then reason: Because every side of a regular hexagon is equal, OA = AC = 2. The interior angles of a regular hexagon are all 120°, therefore in triangle OAC, ∠OAC = 120°, and OA = AC, so triangle OAC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal: ∠COA = ∠OCA = (180° - 120°) / 2 = 30°. Since OA is on the positive x-axis, the polar angle of point C is 30°.
Next find the polar radius OC. Use the law of cosines: OC^2 = OA^2 + AC^2 - 2·OA·AC·cos120° = 2^2 + 2^2 - 2·2·2·(-1/2) = 12, therefore OC = 2√3. Thus the polar coordinates of C are (30°, 2√3).
